hooks.text: The Moon is actually spinning on its axis right now.
You have never seen forty-one percent of the Moon’s surface.
The Moon hides its far side despite spinning at ten miles per hour.

title: Why the Moon Hides its Far Side
description: The Moon isn't frozen; Earth's gravity braked its rotation to match its orbit perfectly through tidal locking.

beats.text: The Moon is actually spinning on its axis right now.
beats.visual: Lick Observatory photograph of the full Moon, 1968

beats.text: Many believe it stays still because we only ever see one face.
beats.visual: LRO mosaic of the lunar near side showing familiar craters, 2011

beats.text: If it didn't rotate, we would see the lunar far side every single month.
beats.visual: LRO mosaic of the lunar far side showing heavily cratered terrain, 2011

beats.text: Instead, Earth’s gravity has spent billions of years braking the Moon’s spin.
beats.visual: Scientific diagram showing Earth's gravitational pull on the Moon

beats.text: This invisible grip created solid tidal bulges, using friction to slow the rotation.
beats.visual: Exaggerated diagram of lunar tidal bulges caused by gravity

beats.text: Now, the Moon completes one rotation in about twenty-seven point three days to match its orbit.
beats.visual: LRO animation of lunar libration showing the rocking motion over one orbit

beats.text: This cosmic anchor is so powerful it even slows Earth’s day by two milliseconds every century.
beats.visual: Diagram of Earth's ocean tides and frictional braking effect

beats.text: Our planet is losing this tug-of-war as the Moon spirals away by four centimeters every year.
beats.visual: Photograph of the Apollo 11 Laser Ranging Retroreflector on the Moon, 1969

beats.text: It is a perpetual, balanced cycle that explains why our neighbor is turning.
beats.visual: DSCOVR EPIC camera view of the Earth and Moon together in space, 2015

better_than_last: Applied rule 23 by structuring the final beat as a complete sentence that leads back to the hook's specific subject while avoiding a repetitive verbatim word match.
